requirement_text.REQ-372:
Filed from a GUI-review sweep applying "review real screens before writing a blind Playwright spec" to test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/platform/definition-type-error-blocked.yaml (test/uat-reports/gui-review-2026-09-20-definition-type-error-blocked.md has the full trace). That scenario's own stale NOTE (ISS-0527) already flagged its pipeline_test as an aspirational forward-reference to a feature never built; this run verified that independently by reading current source rather than trusting the note, and confirms the underlying feature genuinely does not exist, in whole or in part.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY, verified 2026-09-20 by direct source read (not inference): Letflow.Definitions.Graph.validate_edge_conditions/1 (REQ-029) checks structural edge-condition rules (default/condition conflicts, single-default-edge, and -- since REQ-288 -- real CEL grammar validity via Letflow.Engine.Expr.parse_strict/1). None of this resolves a variable NAME against anything: REQ-288's own docstring for the check it replaced states it "never resolves variable names," and REQ-288 itself only tightened syntax/grammar checking, explicitly out of scope for name resolution. Letflow.Engine.VariableSchema (REQ-109) stores each process's declared fields, but a grep of lib/ for any call cross-referencing an authored expression's variable references against VariableSchema returns zero hits outside REQ-291's x-ui vocabulary path (visible_when/computed/cross-field validation on FORM FIELDS only, docs/frontend/ x-ui vocabulary) -- REQ-291's own field-existence check does not run against EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY edge conditions or any task-routing/assignment rule. Letflow.Definitions.Graph.check_* node-attribute validators (REQ-029 CHK-09..12) require a HUMAN_TASK's "role" attribute to be a non-blank STRING, not an expression -- there is no mechanism today for a human-task assignment rule to reference a process field at all, so the scenario's "routes to a reviewer using a field the process does not hold" case has no code path to even reach. Nowhere in lib/letflow/ does any check compare the declared TYPE of two expression operands (e.g. a money-amount field against a customer-name field) -- Expr.parse_strict/1 is untyped; it validates syntax only. web/src's DefinitionEditorPage.tsx / ValidationSummaryBar / per-node canvas annotation plumbing is real and generic (any {nodeId|edgeId, message, severity} renders correctly, per-node annotations already exist for SUB_PROCESS interface errors, REQ-032), but nothing feeds it a field-existence or type-mismatch violation today, and there is no misspelled-field-name suggestion feature (grepped lib/ and web/src for did-you-mean/Levenshtein/nearest-field logic -- no hits).

THIS REQUIREMENT (backend half; a follow-on FRONTEND-DEV requirement, sized once this lands, wires the canvas/problem-list presentation -- same two-step shape as REQ-288 then REQ-291): build the semantic validation pass itself. Given a definition's graph and its VariableSchema-declared fields, for every authored rule expression (EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY edge condition at minimum; decide and record explicitly whether a HUMAN_TASK routing/assignment-by-field mechanism is in scope here or is its own prerequisite gap to file separately -- do not silently assume one way), report ALL violations in one pass (no fix-one-to-see-the-next), each violation naming the offending step/rule and the rule text as authored, for two rule classes: (1) a referenced variable name not present in the process's declared VariableSchema fields -- the violation must name the exact typed string and suggest the nearest declared field name (a real string-distance measure such as Levenshtein against the declared field list, not a placeholder); (2) a comparison between two operands whose declared VariableSchema types are not comparable (e.g. a money/numeric field against a text/string field) -- decide and record explicitly which type pairs are and are not comparable, rather than leaving the boundary implicit. This pass must re-run in full -- not read a cached prior result -- at whatever the definition's actual release/promotion submission call path is (verify at start which function that is; do not assume it is the same validate_definition_graph/2 the draft-save path uses without confirming).

Re-verify at start rather than trusting this description: the current shape of Letflow.Definitions.Graph.validate_edge_conditions/1's Violation struct and call sites (REQ-288 already extended these three: create/2, validate_update_graph/1 under update/2, validate_definition_graph/2 -- confirm they are unchanged), the exact declared-field type vocabulary VariableSchema currently supports, and whether any HUMAN_TASK routing-by-field mechanism has landed under a different name since this filing.

SCOPE FENCE: backend field-existence and type-compatibility checking, its violation shape (including the suggestion string), and re-running it at release-submission time. Does not build the frontend presentation (canvas problem markers, the problem-list UI, or the release-submission re-check screen) -- that is explicitly a follow-on FRONTEND-DEV requirement once this lands, filed the same way REQ-291 followed REQ-288. Does not extend Letflow.Engine.Expr's grammar (REQ-288's closed EXP-102 decision stands unchanged) -- this requirement adds a separate, subsequent semantic pass over an already-parsed expression's referenced names and operand types, not a grammar change.
